expectations.text: Uses the CRA classification tiers: default category, Important Class I, Important Class II, and critical products — and identifies a firewall as an Important product (Class II per Annex III/IV structure)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the firewall as 'most likely... Class I (Annex III)' with Class II only for industrial/OT variants — contradicting the ground truth that a firewall is Important Class II; also misplaces Class II in 'Annex IV' and never mentions the critical-products tier

expectations.text: Explains the conformity-assessment consequence: default products may self-assess (internal control); Class I needs harmonised standards or third-party assessment; Class II requires third-party (notified body) conformity assessment
expectations.evidence: Presents Class I as a free 'choice — Module A self-assessment or Notified Body assessment' without the harmonised-standards condition, and never states that default-category products may self-assess

expectations.text: Covers Annex I essential requirements at a high level (secure-by-default, vulnerability handling, SBOM, support period)
expectations.evidence: 'secure-by-default configuration'; 'Annex I Part II vulnerability handling program: CVD/VDP... SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX)... free security updates for the support period (minimum 5 years)'

expectations.text: Notes CE marking + technical documentation + EU declaration of conformity obligations from the December 11, 2027 application date
expectations.evidence: 'Prepare Annex VII technical documentation'; 'Draw up the EU Declaration of Conformity (Annex V), affix CE marking'; 'ahead of the full CRA application date of 11 December 2027'

expectations.text: Mentions that no CRA harmonised standards are cited in the OJ yet / standards are in development — so conformity planning should not assume a presumption-of-conformity shortcut today
expectations.evidence: No mention of harmonised standards status — nothing about standards not yet cited in the OJ, standards in development, or presumption of conformity
